# Backend pytest signal ledger

Base: `b3c5ff7abb8dd602a1d80d0e2be76c2b86e66cf2`. **5,290 original expanded cases / 3,860 authored templates → 5,284 retained cases / 3,854 templates: 5,284 keep, 0 move, 6 delete.**

Evidence answers: “Has this existing test failed and led to an app-code fix?” [History method and sources](pytest-history.md) distinguish provenance from regression evidence. `No chain established` is a search result, not proof that a test never caught a regression. Each case retains its distinct parameter/input domain. Backend logic already runs at an appropriate cheap seam; no UI-to-unit moves apply.

Keep means an observable API/service/algorithm contract, security/data/concurrency boundary, or release/operator contract. No test is deleted for lacking history alone. Six deletions have named retained coverage and selective red→green controls. Prerequisite skips remain keep and are not claimed as executed coverage. Two retained serial timing checks remain red on audit and pre-audit code, so qualification is incomplete; see [readiness](../BACKEND_READINESS.md). The eight opt-in performance measurements are serial exceptions: shared seeded database mutations and uncontended p95 timing. They run separately with `make perf-titles`.

The initial serial baseline exposed four failures before pruning. Three removed-route tests assumed a built SPA; repaired to verify removal with and without the SPA mount. The temp-directory safety test correctly rejected an invalid runner basetemp; the runner now uses the system temporary directory. These are test/runner environment repairs, not app-code regression evidence.

The seven malformed-caption inputs/assertions are unchanged. Their old byte-derived IDs now use descriptive labels; oversized original IDs are represented by SHA-256 below rather than fixture megabytes. Row identity remains one-to-one.
